correctness.rationale: The metric and polar normalization are explicit. Sorting all N values yields unimodular order chambers; the rank-gap beta CDF gives Lipschitz volume r(2(N-1)-(N-2)r) exactly. The type-A root-polytope facets are products of simplices; their unimodular staircase triangulations and the visible facet count compute Q volume B_N(1/r+(N-2)/(N-1)). The two antipodal added caps lie in opposite halfspaces. The displayed concave quadratic has a unique stationary point in the allowed interval for N>=4, at the endpoint for N=3. Separate exact combinatorial and numerical hull calculations corroborate normalization; no finite computation is substituted for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The 2019 motivating paper solves the equilateral endpoint and proves abstract nonmaximality and a general local cap-volume lemma, not this full single-pair perturbation Mahler profile or the sharp 9/8 gain. The independent-pair published-finding corpus record enumerates facets, a strictly weaker and different statistic. Searches of equivalent root-polytope, one-edge metric, and Wasserstein descriptions found no result implying all displayed formulas. Historical-priority uncertainty is documented, rather than treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An earlier exact volume of a root polytope with one antipodal pair radially displaced may exist under a convex-polytope deformation vocabulary not captured by current searches.
The result is not claimed as a global Mahler extremizer among all N-point metrics, nor over the allowed lengthening interval r>1.
Published search and mathematical argument do not substitute for an independent expert priority or correctness audit.

value.rationale: The motivating 2019 Banach-space Mahler paper identifies global extremal questions and the failure of the equal-weight complete metric to maximize for N>=4. This theorem solves exactly a canonical one-pair metric perturbation in every cardinality, supplies both polar volumes and a unique optimizer, and gives a sharp asymptotic gain of 9/8. These are quantitative structural data not implied by facet counts or the abstract nonmaximality theorem; it is a motivated natural family, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
